notes_en: Fraction effects are in percentage points; IFN effects are mean log1p(counts per 10,000) units.
Original aggregate composition uses 162 SLE and 71 references. Aggregate IFN and the same-population B-fraction sensitivity use 159 SLE and 71 references (>=20 B cells).

Named-state composition uses 155 SLE and 70 references: >=20 total B cells and at least one assigned B_naive/B_mem/B_atypical cell. Five B-positive individuals with wholly unassigned fine labels are unavailable for state composition, not subtype-zero observations. All source B cells, including unresolved cells, remain in denominators.

The common 205-person population consists of 136 SLE and 69 references from the original selected batches with >=20 total B cells, >=20 B_naive cells and >=20 B_mem cells; B_atypical is not required. Both state composition and both state IFN outcomes reuse these same individuals and are not independent samples.
State IFN eligibility is >=20 target-state cells in each individual and >=10 eligible individuals in each arm; B_atypical has only three eligible references and remains unavailable.

BH correction is separate by listed planned family. Unavailable planned tests enter adjustment as P=1 but their q is displayed as unavailable. The original aggregate model is only recalculated for equality; its original FDR family is not replaced.
Coverage diagnostics and the >=90% annotation-coverage analysis were added after source-label review and are not external preregistration. Their outcomes do not imply new cell-level QC.

Unresolved labels are retained and described by condition, processing cohort and batch. Sensitivity populations overlap and are not independent replication; within-state IFN differences do not prove intrinsic activation.
